overview: The committee evaluated funding requests for a community garden pergola and a fire station HVAC project while reviewing a preliminary list of applications for the upcoming fiscal year. Members ultimately denied a request to pivot existing preservation funds toward mechanical upgrades at a city fire station and deferred a garden grant to the regular funding cycle.

items.title: New Member Introduction
items.summary: The committee welcomed new member Ada Gunning.

items.title: Winthrop Street Community Garden Pergola Application
items.summary: Referred the $10,000 pergola project to the regular funding cycle because the request exceeded small grant limits and required more documentation. The committee requested formal vendor quotes and proof of property owner permission from the Department of Conservation and Recreation.

items.title: Fire Station Windows Study Pivot Request
items.summary: Denied a request to reallocate $25,000 of a $75,000 historic window grant to install an HVAC system at the Engine 3 fire station. Members determined that the station lacks historic windows to restore and that the proposed HVAC work did not meet preservation or recreation eligibility requirements.

items.title: Review of Potential FY25 Applications
items.summary: Reviewed a slate of potential projects including City Hall bathroom ADA compliance, Affordable Housing Trust seed money, church envelope repairs, and park improvements. Committee members provided feedback on the eligibility of several proposals, including a use study for the Curtis Tufts school building.

items.title: Routine Business and Meeting Minutes
items.summary: Approved the minutes from the June 11, 2024, meeting and discussed upcoming ribbon-cutting ceremonies for local parks.
